data.summary: The four‑week plan spreads core concepts across all nine units, focusing on foundational ideas early and integrating practice tasks each week. Each week stays within the 5‑hour limit, and the final week uses the live class on equilibrium to review and do timed free‑response practice.

tasks: Read the textbook sections on atomic structure and electron configuration (1.5) and take concise notes (1 hour).
Complete 10 practice problems on electron configuration and periodic trends (1 hour).
Watch a video on types of chemical bonds (2.1) and create a comparison chart (1 hour).
Do 8 free‑response questions on ideal gas law calculations (3.4) and check answers with the solution guide (1 hour).
Solve 5 stoichiometry word problems (4.5), then verify each step using the scoring rubric (1 hour).
Read the section on endothermic and exothermic processes (6.1) and summarize key signs of each (1 hour).
Complete a set of 12 calorimetry calculations (6.4) and compare results to the answer key (1 hour).
Review net ionic equations (4.2) and write balanced net ionic forms for 6 given reactions (1 hour).
Work through 8 rate‑rate problems focusing on reaction rates (5.1) and self‑grade with the scoring guide (1 hour).
Create a one‑page cheat sheet linking energy changes to reaction types (1 hour).

weeks.focus: Equilibrium, acids/bases, and kinetics deeper dive
tasks: Read about equilibrium constants (7.3) and solve 10 problems calculating Kc from concentrations (1 hour).
Do a set of 8 pH/pOH calculations for strong acids and bases (8.2) and check work against the guide (1 hour).
Watch a tutorial on introduction to rate law (5.2) and write the rate law for 5 sample reactions (1 hour).
Solve 6 Gibbs free‑energy problems (9.3) and annotate each step with the relevant equation (1 hour).
Mix the four topics in a 20‑minute timed mini‑quiz of 4 mixed free‑response questions, then grade using the rubric (1 hour).

weeks.focus: Mixed review and timed practice using live class
tasks: Attend live class 9900 (week 4) on equilibrium introduction (7.1) and take detailed notes (1 hour).
Complete 6 free‑response questions on acid‑base reactions and buffers (8.4) under timed conditions (1 hour).
Work through 5 problems on galvanic and electrolytic cells (9.4) and self‑grade (1 hour).
Do 4 elementary reaction mechanism problems (5.4) and compare solutions with the answer key (1 hour).
Run a 30‑minute full‑length timed practice set containing 2 questions from each unit covered so far, then review mistakes and note any lingering gaps (1 hour).

data.final_week_advice: After the four‑week sprint, focus on timed full‑exam practice, review the cheat sheets you created, and revisit any topics where errors persisted. Use the AP exam released questions to simulate test conditions and refine your pacing.
